issues.title: Generic calendar suffix filtering includes disabled providers
issues.description: The getGenericCalendarSuffixes() method uses Object.keys(GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES) to iterate over all providers defined in the constant, including office365_calendar. However, getProviders() only returns ['google_calendar'], meaning Office365 is not actually enabled. This causes the subscription system to filter out Office365 calendar suffixes even when Office365 calendars shouldn't be processed at all. The filtering should only include suffixes for enabled providers by using this.getProviders() as in the original implementation.

issues.title: Empty suffix array incorrectly bypasses generic calendar filtering
issues.description: The filtering logic adds a length check (genericCalendarSuffixes?.length) that treats an empty array as falsy, setting AND to undefined instead of an empty array. In Prisma, AND: undefined means no filtering, while AND: [] also means no filtering but with different semantics. More critically, this breaks the filtering for providers like office365_calendar that have an empty suffix list in GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES. The double optional chaining (?. used twice) is redundant and the length check changes the behavior from the intended design where empty arrays should still be processed.

issues.title: Incomplete class rename breaks all imports and causes runtime failures
issues.description: The class was renamed from SelectedCalendarRepository to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository (line 5) without providing a backward-compatible export alias. This breaks all existing code that imports this class. The test file within this PR (SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts:2,50,53) still imports and instantiates the old class name, causing test failures. Production code in apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts:41 and apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts:61 also use 'new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)' which will fail at runtime with a TypeError indicating SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26774 - feat: CalendarCache - filter generic calendars from subscription batch

structured_output.summary:
The PR keeps Google generic calendars (holiday, contacts, shared, imported, resource) out of the calendar-subscription batch. It adds a GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES map and getGenericCalendarSuffixes() on the adapter factory, passes those suffixes from CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions into findNextSubscriptionBatch, and applies one NOT endsWith clause per suffix in Prisma. The filtering approach is sound and the service and repository tests cover the new parameter.

The PR also renames the concrete class SelectedCalendarRepository to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository without updating its consumers. The cron route and the calendar-subscription webhook route still import and instantiate the old name, and the repository test still imports it. That fails type-checking, and at runtime the cron route throws before doing any subscription work.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The class rename is a breaking change the diff does not carry through. Two production routes and the repository's own test still construct SelectedCalendarRepository, so the subscription cron fails on every run. Once the rename is reverted or the call sites are updated, the remaining items are maintainability and test-quality concerns.

architecture.overview: Calendar subscriptions are driven by CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions, which the cron route apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts invokes. The service asks the selected-calendar repository for up to 100 rows that still need a subscription (never subscribed, or channel expired) for the enabled providers and teams, then subscribes each one. The adapter factory supplies the provider list. This PR adds a generic-calendar suffix list to the factory and threads it through the service into a Prisma NOT endsWith filter, so holiday, contact, shared, imported, and resource calendars are excluded from the batch. The same PR renames the repository class, which the consuming routes do not yet reflect.
steps: Entry point: the cron route constructs DefaultAdapterFactory and the repository, then calls checkForNewSubscriptions.
Factory: GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES in AdaptersFactory.ts lists Google suffixes per provider, and getGenericCalendarSuffixes() flattens them into one list.
Service: checkForNewSubscriptions in CalendarSubscriptionService.ts passes that list as genericCalendarSuffixes to findNextSubscriptionBatch.
Repository: PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository.findNextSubscriptionBatch adds one AND NOT externalId endsWith clause per suffix; the class rename is the change that leaves callers broken.

findings.title: Class rename breaks production routes and the repository test
findings.fixPrompt: The class in packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts was renamed to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository, which breaks its consumers. Either restore the class name SelectedCalendarRepository on line 5, or update every reference. The references are: apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts (import on line 11, usage on line 41), apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts (import on line 14, usage on line 61), and packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts (import on line 3, usage on lines 50 and 53). Keep the rest of the PR unchanged and run the repository and service tests afterwards.

findings.title: Generic suffix list is flattened across all providers
findings.fixPrompt: In packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts, getGenericCalendarSuffixes() (lines 67-71) flattens GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES across all providers, so Google suffixes also filter Office 365 subscriptions. Consider changing the method to take a provider argument, for example getGenericCalendarSuffixes(provider: CalendarSubscriptionProvider), and returning GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES[provider]. Update the AdapterFactory interface (line 25), the call in CalendarSubscriptionService.ts that passes the suffixes per integration, and the test mock. Keep the behavior identical for Google.

findings.title: Optional suffix parameter silently disables the filter
findings.fixPrompt: In packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.interface.ts, the findNextSubscriptionBatch parameter genericCalendarSuffixes (line 35) is optional, so omitting it silently drops the generic-calendar filter. Make it required, string[] with no question mark. Update the matching declaration in SelectedCalendarRepository.ts (line 27) so it is also required. Then check that the existing tests in SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts that call findNextSubscriptionBatch without the argument pass an explicit array. Keep the Prisma AND behavior for an empty array unchanged.

findings.title: Redundant optional chaining and no-op AND: undefined assertions
findings.fixPrompt: In packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts lines 41-45, replace genericCalendarSuffixes?.map with genericCalendarSuffixes.map, since the length check above already narrows the value. In packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts, remove the three `AND: undefined,` lines (134, 164, 194) that were added to existing expectations, since they add nothing to toHaveBeenCalledWith.

findings.title: Tests cover the query shape but not the empty-array or Office 365 paths
findings.fixPrompt: Add coverage for the generic-calendar filter. In packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts, add a case where genericCalendarSuffixes is an empty array and assert that the where clause has no AND key. Also add a unit test for DefaultAdapterFactory in packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts that asserts getGenericCalendarSuffixes() returns the four Google suffixes and no duplicates. Follow the existing test style in the repository test file.

findings.title: Existing generic subscriptions are not cleaned up on rollout
findings.fixPrompt: In packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/CalendarSubscriptionService.ts, checkForNewSubscriptions (lines 391-397) now excludes generic calendars from the batch. Confirm and document in the PR or code comment that already-subscribed generic calendars are not unsubscribed. Their channels lapse at channelExpiration and are not renewed. If an explicit cleanup is needed, add it as a separate task and do not rely on this filter for it.

findings.title: Filter is scoped to exactly the Google suffixes and wired through the factory
findings.body: The suffix list lives in one exported constant, and the service receives it through the existing adapter-factory dependency instead of reaching for a global. That keeps the service testable, and the mock in the service test shows the seam is easy to use. The Prisma NOT endsWith clause is also a good fit for the filter, because the suffixes are exact domain tails and the query stays in the database.
